title: Early Muslim conquests
summary: After the Prophet Muhammad's death in 632 CE, the Rashidun caliphs launched campaigns into Byzantine and Sasanian lands, as both empires had exhausted themselves in constant war. Rashidun forces crushed the Byzantines at Yarmouk in 636, drove them from the Levant, took Egypt, and conquered the Sasanian Empire by 651. The conquest of most of Iran proved permanent: Islam eventually spread among Iranians, and Arabic became the language of religion, literature and science there.

uncertainty.note: Campaigns began under Abu Bakr upon Muhammad's death in 632 CE; the initial wave of conquest under the Rashidun Caliphate concluded with Ali's death in 661 CE, while subsequent Umayyad expansions continued until roughly 750 CE.
